result.title: PrivMeSA: Privacy-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Medicine via Local-Remote LLM Collaboration
result.summary: Clinical large language model (LLM) agents deployed locally can consult more capable remote models, but doing so risks exposing patient information. Privacy-conscious delegation places disclosure decisions with a local agent, yet removing explicit identifiers is insufficient: quasi-identifiers can accumulate across multi-turn consultations and repeated patient visits to enable re-identification. We introduce PrivMeSA, a privacy-aware self-evolving multi-agent system that learns to control disclosure and retains remote expertise for local reuse. A local agent manages each encounter and consults remote specialists that may request additional information. Reinforcement learning balances task accuracy against direct disclosure and registry-based re-identification risk, with privacy evaluated over the complete outbound transcript of each encounter. A local lesson memory distills completed consultations into generalized clinical guidance and retrieves relevant lessons before transmission, allowing subsequent cases to reuse expertise without another remote exchange. Memory grows without additional outcome labels or parameter updates. On an emergency-department benchmark built from MIMIC-IV-ED records, PrivMeSA improves mean task accuracy over delegation by up to 15.8 percentage points. In the same setting, PrivMeSA reduces the disclosure of personal details from 98.0% to 0.2% of cases and the share of cases in which the patient can be narrowed to ten or fewer registry patients from 74% to 0%.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 PrivMeSA，一个隐私感知的自演化多智能体医疗系统：本地 LLM 智能体决定向远程专家披露多少信息，用强化学习在任务准确率与直接披露、基于登记库的重识别风险之间权衡，并把完成的会诊蒸馏为本地经验记忆供后续复用。在 MIMIC-IV-ED 急诊基准上报告了准确率与隐私指标改善。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究重点是临床多智能体的信息披露控制与隐私风险权衡，虽涉及多轮会诊中的信息累积与记忆复用，但不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、证据筛选、latent 轨迹或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的方法线索。
